items.stem: Explain why a function can be positive but decreasing.
items.answer: Being positive is about the value f(x) > 0, whereas decreasing depends on the gradient f′(x) < 0; e.g. f(x) = 1/x for x > 0 is positive and decreasing.
items.markingKey: B1 value vs gradient; B1 example [2]

items.stem: Explain how to show that a function is increasing for all real x.
items.answer: Find f′(x) and show it is positive for every x, e.g. by completing the square to get a(x + p)² + q with a > 0 and q > 0.
items.markingKey: B1 f′(x) > 0 for all x; B1 method such as completing the square or discriminant < 0 [2]

items.stem: Leila says that the curve y = x² + 10x + 16 has stationary points at x = −8 and x = −2, because y = 0 there. Explain the error and find the stationary point.
items.answer: Stationary points need dy/dx = 0, not y = 0 (those are the x-intercepts). dy/dx = 2x + 10 = 0 gives the stationary point (−5, −9).
items.markingKey: B1 stationary means dy/dx = 0; B1 (−5, −9)

items.stem: Show that the function f(x) = x³ + 3x² + 6x − 5 is increasing for all values of x.
items.answer: f′(x) = 3x² + 6x + 6 = 3(x + 1)² + 3 > 0 for all x, so f is increasing.
items.markingKey: M1 f′(x) = 3x² + 6x + 6; M1 completes the square 3(x + 1)² + 3 (or discriminant < 0); A1 > 0 for all x, conclusion

items.stem: Explain why the second derivative test fails at the stationary point of y = x⁴ at the origin, and how its nature can still be found.
items.answer: d²y/dx² = 12x² = 0 at x = 0, so the test gives no conclusion; checking the gradient on either side (negative then positive) shows it is a minimum.

items.stem: Explain, in terms of the gradient, why d²y/dx² < 0 at a stationary point gives a maximum.
items.answer: d²y/dx² < 0 means the gradient is decreasing; it passes from positive to zero to negative, so the curve rises then falls: a maximum.
items.markingKey: B1 gradient decreasing; B1 positive to negative so maximum [2]

items.stem: Explain why it is important to check the domain when solving a practical maximum problem.
items.answer: The variable represents a physical quantity (e.g. a length), so only values in a realistic range are valid; a stationary point outside it, or an end point, may give the true answer.
items.markingKey: B1 physical restrictions on the variable; B1 check end points / reject invalid values [2]

items.markingKey: M1 f′(x) = 3x² + 18x + 36; M1 completes the square 3(x + 3)² + 9 (or discriminant < 0); A1 > 0 for all x, conclusion

items.stem: Show that the function f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 15x − 4 is increasing for all values of x.
items.answer: f′(x) = 3x² − 12x + 15 = 3(x − 2)² + 3 > 0 for all x, so f is increasing.
items.markingKey: M1 f′(x) = 3x² − 12x + 15; M1 completes the square 3(x − 2)² + 3 (or discriminant < 0); A1 > 0 for all x, conclusion

Grace uses 150 m of fencing for three sides of a rectangular enclosure beside a long wall in Seoul. Each side perpendicular to the wall has length x m. Show that the area A m² is A = 150x − 2x², and explain why 0 < x < 75.
items.answer: The side parallel to the wall is 150 − 2x, so A = x(150 − 2x) = 150x − 2x². Both x and 150 − 2x must be positive, so 0 < x < 75.
items.markingKey: B1 side 150 − 2x and A = 150x − 2x²; B1 lengths positive so 0 < x < 75

(c) Find the maximum area, correct to 3 significant figures, and show that it is a maximum.
items.markingKey: (a) M1 A = xy + πx²/8; A1 simplifies to given form [2] (b) M1 dA/dx = 5 − (4 + π)x/4 = 0; A1 2.80 [2] (c) B1 d²A/dx² = −(4 + π)/4 < 0; A1 7.00 m² [2]

items.stem: Oil spreads in a circular patch on water near Lagos. The radius increases at 4 cm s⁻¹. Noah says dA/dt = πr² × 4 = 36π cm² s⁻¹ when r = 3. Explain the error and find the correct rate.
items.answer: Noah multiplied the area, not its derivative dA/dr = 2πr, by dr/dt. dA/dt = 2π × 3 × 4 = 24π cm² s⁻¹.
items.markingKey: B1 must use dA/dr = 2πr; B1 24π
